paragraphs: Meet Our Pen Pals, posted by Lily. Our pen pals are in Ms. Ong's class in Singapore. They are eleven, the same age as the Explorers. Ms. Ong and Teacher Kim started the pen-pal project together. We write emails to them every month. Now I want to tell you about four of them. Each child has different likes and a different character.

Grace writes to me, and she likes drawing and music. She draws comics and plays the violin. Her violin is not expensive, but she loves it. Grace is a little shy and very polite. She draws her feelings in her comics. Her emails are short, but they are always kind. Last month, she drew a comic about a cat who plays music.

Ravi writes to Leo, and he likes cooking and badminton. He sends Leo a new recipe every month. Ravi wants to play for the national team one day. He is friendly and funny, so everybody likes him. He practices badminton every day after school. In his last email, Ravi wrote about a big match. Leo says, "Ravi is the funniest pen pal!"

Alex is a friend of my brother Tom, and he likes robots and football. He also plays computer games. In his last email, Alex wrote about a new robot. It can pick up a small ball. His robot kit was expensive, so he keeps it safe. Alex is serious and careful. He has a green belt in judo, and he practices on Sunday. He explains things in a clear way, like a teacher.

Nadia writes to Mia, and she likes animals, swimming, and photos. Her photos are clear and beautiful. Last week, she sent Mia a photo of a dog near the sea. Mia keeps it on her desk. She is brave, because she is not afraid of big dogs. Mia thinks that Nadia is the same as her in many ways. They all write about their days, and we learn a lot from them. I like all four pen pals, but they are not the same. Which pen pal do you want to meet?
text.summary: Lily writes a page for Explorers' Blog about four pen pals in Singapore. For each child, the page says what the child likes and what the child is like.
